question: Who is the Indian batsman after whom the Ranji Trophy is named?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ranjit Sinhji**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Ranji Trophy is named after **Ranjit Sinhji**, who was one of the first Indian cricketers to gain international fame.
 
• Ranjit Sinhji, also known as "Ranji," played for the English cricket team and is considered one of the greatest batsmen of all time.
 
• He was the ruler of the princely state of Nawanagar and was known for his unique batting style and contributions to cricket.
 
• The Ranji Trophy, India's premier domestic cricket competition, was established in 1934 to honor his legacy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ranjit Sinhji** was born on 10th September 1872 and passed away on 2nd April 1933.
 
• He played for Sussex in English county cricket and for Cambridge University.
 
• Ranjit Sinhji was the first Indian to play Test cricket, debuting for England in 1896.
 
• His innovative technique and prolific run-scoring made him a cricketing legend.
 
• The Ranji Trophy continues to be a crucial platform for aspiring cricketers in India to showcase their talent.
